user.title: Selectronic SP PRO
user.description: Connect to the Selectronic SP PRO add-on's API. Inside Home Assistant the host is `local-selpi`; the token is in the add-on's /data/api_token (normally discovery fills this in for you).

hassio_confirm.title: Selectronic SP PRO
hassio_confirm.description: Add the SP PRO from the {addon} add-on?

reauth_confirm.title: Selectronic SP PRO (API token)
reauth_confirm.description: The add-on refused the token. Enter the one in the add-on's /data/api_token.

error.cannot_connect: Can't reach the Selectronic SP PRO add-on (or it can't reach the SP PRO).

abort.already_configured: This SP PRO is already set up.
abort.cannot_connect: Can't reach the Selectronic SP PRO add-on.

init.title: Polling
init.description: How often to ask the add-on for new values. The fast poll covers only the live power/voltage/frequency/SoC readings; everything else uses the main interval. Suggested main interval for this connection: {suggested} s (Select.Live is a cloud round trip each time: keep the main interval at 60 s or more; the fast poll keeps the link warm, so it can go lower).

data.fast_scan_interval: Fast poll interval for live power/voltage/frequency/SoC (seconds)
data.grace: Keep last values this many seconds before entities go unavailable (0 = go unavailable immediately)
data.esp_present: Also running the ESPHome component (hide its duplicate SP PRO data sensors)

esp_clock_conflict.title: SP PRO clock synced by both the add-on and the ESP
esp_clock_conflict.description: The selpi add-on and the ESPHome component are both set to sync the SP PRO clock. With the ESP present, turn off the add-on's clock sync (set SELPI_CLOCK_SYNC=false in the add-on config) so only one writes the clock.
